text:
maria: Ran a couple of nsys traces on the canary runtime after the driver bump, seeing a weird stall during kernel selection + KV cache apply. Putting notes here in case others hit it.

kevin: which nsys + driver versions? saw something similar last month with old CUPTI.

maria: nsys 2023.5.1, driver 535.86 -> previous working was 525.*. CUPTI callbacks show a ~200ms gap where we expect kernel launch. The timeline shows 'futex' long waits in the worker threads.

chris: futex waits often indicate a userland lock contended path. Could be our batching heuristic locking the kvcache. Do you have the perf timeline link?

maria: perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/#!inspect?traces=redwood/canary-180770 -> (private) short summary inline: main host thread issues kernel selection, then 2 worker threads hit futex wait ~10-10.2s, no CUpti activity for ~180ms, then a big spike when kernels finally submitted.

kevin: can you paste the nsys collect command and the small stack snippet? might be helpful.

maria: command: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=canary-180770 nsys-run.sh ./runtime_test --model=redwood-v1``` stack (from host threads): ```#0 futex_wait #1 pthread_mutex_lock #2 kvcache::apply_prefix_lock #3 batcher::dispatch```

chris: that 'apply_prefix_lock' is new from the kvcache refactor, but never saw long futex before. Could driver change have altered scheduling/prioritization so kernels queue differently?

maria: also saw lots of "CUPTI callback delayed" messages in nsys metadata (attached). Permissions note: when I ran nsys as non-root inside the canary container the kernel timeline was missing CUPTI markers. Running as root gave full markers. devex-bot said we should avoid root in CI.

devex-bot: FYI, CUPTI requires proper driver-backed user-space components; in containers you need CAP_SYS_PTRACE or the container must mount /proc/sys/kernel/yama* (see ticket #412).

kevin: hmm. Two actionable things: 1) reproduce with rootless & CAP_SYS_PTRACE to see if missing markers change behavior; 2) try pinning nsys to 2022.x or rolling driver to 525 to see if regression is driver-related. If only appears with 535.*, likely driver bug.

chris: agree. Also add a microbench: single-request dispatch with kvcache disabled to see if futex still shows. If it disappears, we're hitting a lock-contention path in batching.

maria: did a quick microbench: with kvcache disabled stall drops from ~200ms to <5ms. So kvcache lock seems correlated. However, the lock held time reported by perf is tiny; the long futex is a wait-for-notify rather than long hold. Suggests a scheduler preemption or delayed kernel enqueue.

kevin: driver hangs can cause delayed submission; there were release notes about 'stream scheduling changes' in 535.*. Could cause long gaps between submission and kernel start, making the host threads wait on completions.

chris: run nsys with the "cuda:kernel" detailed trace (lower level) and capture the nvml counters. Also try CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to see if behavior changes (not a fix, but diagnostic).

maria: ran with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -> latency increased overall but futex stall went away. That implies asynchronous submission ordering is part of the issue.

kevin: ok that narrows it. Plan: (A) open an internal bug with NVIDIA with the trace and a minimal repro (we need to craft a tiny loop that reproduces with kvcache interactions), (B) pin driver to 525 for the canary pool and run soak, (C) add temporary canary config to disable kvcache lock coalescing heuristic in runtime so we reduce contention.

chris: for (C) can we expose an env flag to switch batching heuristics at runtime? Should be a quick toggle to try in production. If it works, we can do A/B canary to confirm.

maria: I'll push a toggle in the canary image tonight and start a soak run. Also will attach the nsys .qdrep and the small reproducer sketch.

devex-bot: Reminder: when uploading traces, strip tokens and customer data; attach internal ticket ID once created.

kevin: who will open the NVIDIA ticket? I can file since I have the partner NDA contact. Need the qdrep, perfetto link, and reproducer.

maria: assigning to kevin. I'll upload artifacts to /internal/traces/180770.

chris: one more note — Dedicated fleet saw fewer occurrences. Possibly GPU driver versions differ there; good to check kernel+driver on both fleets.

kevin: noted. I'll also add a small regression alert: if per-request p99 latency jumps >50ms after driver bumps, auto-disable kvcache coalescing in canary via the rollout controller.

maria: thanks team. I'll post updates here after the soak and once the repro is attached to the ticket. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy monitor: canary-runtime-soak started at 1807710000. Watch SLO dashboard for latency spikes.
